item.title: Deploying Grafana
item.description:
Grafana is a visualization and alerting service. A production deployment needs more than a running container: it needs durable state, reproducible provisioning, authenticated access, and a backup and upgrade procedure.

Run Grafana with Persistent State #

Grafana stores users, dashboards created in the UI, alerting data, and configuration metadata in its database. For a small installation, persist the default SQLite database; for highly available deployments, use a supported external database and run multiple Grafana instances behind a load balancer.

item.title: Loki and Elasticsearch
item.description:
Loki and Elasticsearch can both store and query logs, but they make different tradeoffs. Elasticsearch indexes the contents of each document, enabling fast and flexible full-text search. Loki primarily indexes labels and leaves the log contents compressed in chunks, reducing indexing cost while encouraging queries that first select a small set of log streams.

This article explains Loki, introduces LogQL, and compares Loki with Elasticsearch as a log platform.

item.title: Prometheus and PromQL
item.description:
• Prometheus for metrics
  • Loki or Elasticsearch for logs • Tempo or Jaeger for traces • Grafana as a unified interface

Prometheus is a monitoring system built around time-series data. It periodically scrapes metrics from applications, stores the samples locally, and provides PromQL (Prometheus Query Language) for querying them. Grafana can use Prometheus as a data source and turn the same queries into dashboards.

This article explains the Prometheus data model and the PromQL patterns needed for day-to-day monitoring.
